title: Reliable webhook delivery
learning_objectives: Propose and revise an inspectable architecture
problem_statement: Deliver outbound webhooks for 500 tenants at 1200 events per second, with retries retained for seven days and observable per-delivery state.

progressive_constraints.title: Durable acknowledgement
progressive_constraints.description: Acknowledge an event only after its pending delivery state is durable.

progressive_constraints.title: Noisy neighbor
progressive_constraints.description: One tenant waits 29 seconds per call; bound tenant concurrency or schedule fairly.

progressive_constraints.title: Pause and replay
progressive_constraints.description: A tenant pauses delivery then replays six hours. Keep stable delivery identities and a replay log.

progressive_constraints.title: Retention and failover
progressive_constraints.description: Estimate the retained retry payload and explicitly bound acknowledged-event loss on failover.

valid_architecture_families.name: Partitioned broker with delivery log
valid_architecture_families.description: Queue lanes and durable delivery records isolate retries and tenants.

valid_architecture_families.name: Tenant-sharded SQL outbox
valid_architecture_families.description: SQLite WAL/NVMe or SQL SKIP LOCKED can be defensible within declared capacity and durability limits; no Kafka brand requirement.

common_misconceptions: A single FIFO worker pool lets slow tenants monopolize capacity.
Async replication does not imply zero acknowledged-event loss.

hint_ladder.level_1: Trace a fast tenant arriving behind a slow endpoint.
hint_ladder.level_2: Compare partitioned broker lanes with fair polling of SQL outbox rows.
hint_ladder.level_3: At 1200 events/sec over seven days there are 725760000 event slots before retention reduction. Multiply by declared bytes per event and replication; then explain duplicate identity and the allowed failover RPO.

consolidation: Webhook design separates acceptance durability, scheduling fairness, effect identity, replay and retention. SQLite-per-tenant is a valid candidate, while its actual throughput and recovery must be evidenced rather than asserted.
fresh_transfer_question: What if a tenant requires strict per-object ordering but permits parallel delivery across different objects?
coach_instructions: One clear question at a time. Inspect actual graph and stated assumptions. Do not grade prose by keywords or require a vendor name. Numeric assumptions are learner declarations, not measured performance. Explain when asked, require teach-back, and preserve alternative valid designs. Do not silently edit the diagram.
